papers.version_note: arXiv:2209.14405v1, dated September 30, 2022 on the first page; the text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A preprint that proposes the Lie rank of the dynamical Lie algebra as a design metric for Pauli-based variational circuits and tests it on a 2 x 2 XXZ-Heisenberg model.

existing.note: The abstract sentence holds, but the body limits it: the only application is one 2 x 2 XXZ-Heisenberg system, the Conclusion calls the work preliminary explorations, and the energy experiment compares the VHA with the LAP energy by parameter count and layers, not Lie rank against energy directly. The LAP ansatz, with the full Lie algebra, reached only -1.0721 against a ground state energy of -1.9794.
existing.value: The authors report, from numerical experiments on one XXZ-Heisenberg model, that the Lie rank criterion positively correlates with the ability of the Pauli-based ansatz to approximate ground-state energies, and describe this as preliminary explorations.
existing.anchor: Abstract p.1; Section V Conclusion p.9
quotes: Through numerical experiments, we ﬁnd that the Lie rank criterion of the Hamiltonian that deﬁnes the system ansatz positively correlates with the ability of the Pauli-based ansatz to approximate ground-state energies.

papers.what_it_is: A preprint (arXiv 2605.00107v1, 30 Apr 2026) that defines seven mutation operations for quantum neural networks and a directed generation approach, and compares them with prior gate-level mutation operations on simulated QNN and QCNN models.

For images, it also uses cropping, rotating, horizontal flipping and vertical flipping.
quotes: Therefore, we can directly alter features of the input data sample to cause a mutation in the data sample feature change (DFC) mutation operation.

assertions.value: The authors state that, among popular one-qubit parameterized gates, RX and RY change the amplitude whereas RZ adjusts the phase shift, and that APGC targets a change to a parameterized gate with a different impact on the qubit value.
quotes: RX (θ) and RY (θ) causes the amplitude to change, whereas RZ(θ) adjusts the phase shift.

assertions.value: The authors define layer shuffling (LS) as switching two layers, plus in-layer shuffles such as placing the entangling gates before the rotation gates; in-layer shuffling (ILS) swaps blocks inside a layer. Layer addition (ALA) adds a layer after existing layers, with parameters set by random initialization or by copying another layer's weights. Layer deletion (ALD) removes the entire layer, the rotation gates only, or the entangling gates only.

papers.what_it_is: A theory-plus-simulation paper that defines contextual recurrent neural networks (CRNNs, Gaussian operations on a GKP state with non-Gaussian Pauli phase measurements), proves a memory lower bound for locally Lipschitz classical sequence models on a stabilizer measurement translation task, and compares classically simulated CRNNs with classical models on a Spanish-to-English translation data set.

papers.title_in_file: Experimental evidence of generalization in quantum machine learning in small-data regime
